title: RBAC v2 taxonomy: resources/actions/scopes + naming conventions (Hosted/Dedicated/Private examples)
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Goal
Define the RBAC v2 permission taxonomy and naming conventions used across Redwood Inference (control plane APIs, console backend routes, admin/support tooling, and private deployment admin flows). This should be unambiguous, stable over time, and easy to map from endpoints.

Context
RBAC v1 has feature-gated and inconsistent checks across services. RBAC v2 is moving to a consistent model:
- Permission = (resource, action, scope)
- Evaluation is centralized and consistent across gateway/service/console backends
- Policies ship in the policy bundle repo and need a stable vocabulary

Deliverable
A written taxonomy + conventions that:
1) Defines canonical resource types + hierarchy (org/project/deployment/etc)
2) Defines a standard action verb set with semantics
3) Defines how scope is represented and when it is required
4) Provides concrete examples for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
5) Provides guidance for naming new permissions and reviewing changes

Proposal (v0)

A) Permission identifier format
We will represent permissions internally as structured fields (resource/action/scope), and in policy bundles as a canonical string:

permission_id := "<scope>.<resource>.<action>"
- scope: org | project | deployment | system (support-only) | cluster (Dedicated internal)
- resource: snake_case noun, singular, may include subresource segments with double-underscore
- action: verb from the standard verb set below

Examples:
- org.api_key.create
- project.model_rollout.update
- org.sso_settings.update
- deployment.policy_bundle.update (Private)
- cluster.gpu_pool.update (Dedicated)

Rationale:
- String is stable + readable for audits, tickets, and inventory sheets
- Still supports structured evaluation (the string is just the canonical representation)

B) Resource naming conventions
Rules:
1) Resource names are nouns; singular; snake_case.
2) Use subresources to avoid inventing new top-level resources for small surfaces.
   Format: <parent>__<child> (double underscore)
   Example: org__member, org__role_assignment
3) Avoid embedding environment/tier in the resource unless the object truly exists only in that tier.
   Prefer: deployment, capacity, gpu_pool as resources; tier differences handled via scope + availability.
4) Avoid duplicating scope words in resource names.
   Good: org.sso_settings.update
   Avoid: org.organization_settings.update

Initial resource set (not exhaustive; intended to cover most control plane/console surfaces)
Org-scope resources
- org_settings
- org_member
- org_invite
- role
- role_assignment
- audit_log
- audit_log_export
- sso_settings
- api_key
- billing_account
- billing_invoice
- usage_report
- webhook

Project-scope resources
- project_settings
- project_member
- secret
- model
- model_version
- model_rollout
- eval_set
- prompt_set
- routing_policy

Deployment/Dedicated/Private resources
- deployment_settings
- capacity_reservation (Dedicated)
- gpu_pool (Dedicated)
- autoscaling_policy (Dedicated)
- private_installer (Private admin plane)
- policy_bundle (Private)
- kms_integration (Private)

Support/system resources (strictly limited)
- support_impersonation_session
- break_glass_session
- customer_tenant

C) Standard action verb set
Verbs should be consistent across resources; we can constrain and extend as needed.

Baseline verbs
- read: view/list/get metadata (non-sensitive by default, but some resources are always sensitive)
- create: create new resource
- update: modify existing resource configuration
- delete: delete resource

Operational verbs (explicit)
- rotate: rotate a key/secret (for api_key/secret)
- revoke: revoke/disable (api_key)
- enable / disable: feature toggles or auth methods (sso_settings)
- export: exporting data out of Redwood (audit_log_export, usage_report)
- run: execute an operation (eval_set.run, prompt_set.run) when it has cost/side effects
- deploy: publish/rollout change (model_rollout.deploy)

Support/admin-only verbs
- impersonate: support impersonation entry point
- grant: grant elevated session / break-glass
- approve: approval actions in workflows

Notes:
- Prefer update vs set_* actions. Use explicit verbs only when the side effect is meaningful or sensitive (rotate/revoke/export/impersonate/grant).
- Avoid “write” as a verb; use create/update/delete.

D) Scope semantics
Scope describes what boundary the permission is evaluated at. Policy evaluation will consider:
- the actor’s membership/role at that scope
- the target object’s scope owner (e.g., api_key belongs to org)

Scope rules:
1) Every permission MUST declare exactly one scope.
2) The scope should be the narrowest boundary that matches where roles are assigned.
   Examples:
   - org.api_key.create (org roles)
   - project.model_rollout.deploy (project roles)
3) deployment scope is used for actions limited to a particular deployment instance (especially Private).
4) system scope is reserved for internal support actions and cannot be granted via customer-managed roles.

E) Examples by tier
Hosted (SaaS) examples
- org.api_key.create / org.api_key.rotate / org.api_key.revoke / org.api_key.read
- org.audit_log.read
- org.audit_log_export.create (export is sensitive; not implied by audit_log.read)
- org.sso_settings.update / org.sso_settings.read
- billing_account.read / billing_account.update

Dedicated examples
- cluster.gpu_pool.read / cluster.gpu_pool.update
- cluster.autoscaling_policy.read / cluster.autoscaling_policy.update
- org.capacity_reservation.read / org.capacity_reservation.update (customer-facing contract config)
- project.routing_policy.update (if routing policy affects a dedicated deployment)

Private (VPC/on-prem) examples
- deployment.policy_bundle.read / deployment.policy_bundle.update (bundle updates via installer/admin)
- deployment.kms_integration.update
- deployment.private_installer.run (invoking upgrade/reconfigure)
- org.audit_log_export.create (if export endpoints exist in private control plane, scoped appropriately)

Support-only examples (system scope)
- system.support_impersonation_session.create (enter impersonation)
- system.break_glass_session.grant (granting elevated time-bounded access)
- system.customer_tenant.read (lookup tenant metadata for debugging)

F) Required metadata when adding a new permission
For each new permission_id, the owner must provide:
- permission_id
- description (human-readable; used in console UI + audits)
- sensitivity: P0/P1/P2 (per inventory rubric)
- scope (org/project/deployment/system/cluster)
- resources touched (data classification if applicable)
- default roles allowed (or explicit note: “no default roles”)
- audit log expectations (must produce allow/deny decision context)

Out of scope for this ticket
- Final decision on allow/deny semantics in the policy engine (tracked in ADR-014)
- UI strings for console role management (DES-241)
- Enumerating the full permission inventory list (ENG-5382 + inventory sheet)

Open questions
1) Do we treat Dedicated “cluster” as a first-class scope or model it as org/deployment with attributes?
   - Current proposal keeps "cluster" only for internal dedicated infrastructure actions where roles are assigned at that layer.
2) Do we need region scope for multi-region Hosted deployments?
   - Likely no for v0; keep as attribute-based constraints in routing policy later.
3) Should we keep “deployment” scope for Hosted at all?
   - Only if we later expose per-deployment admin; today most Hosted is org/project.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Conventions agreed by Security Eng + Control Plane owners (Marcus/Kaitlyn/Ethan) and API reviewer (Brian)
- [ ] Taxonomy section pasted/linked into RBAC v2 overview doc
- [ ] ENG-5382 inventory crawler produces proposed permission_ids that match conventions without ad-hoc mapping
- [ ] Policy bundle PR template updated to reference this taxonomy (owner checklist)

Links
- Confluence: RBAC v2 overview (WIP)
- ADR-014: policy format + evaluation semantics (in review)
- ENG-5382: inventory crawler/script (dependency)

Proposed next steps
1) Brian + Kaitlyn: sanity check naming against control plane endpoint patterns (especially API keys, SSO, billing, audit logs).
2) Chloe: verify console backend route grouping maps cleanly to these scopes/resources.
3) Jordan: add a short “common pitfalls” section once we see output from ENG-5382.
comments:
2025-02-05 — Kaitlyn Nguyen:
Pulled a sample of control-plane endpoints (keys, org settings, rollouts). The "scope.resource.action" format is workable. One request: allow subresources for member operations (org__member) so we can avoid org_member_invite as separate nouns.

Also: for rollouts we should distinguish "model_rollout.deploy" vs "model_rollout.update". Deploy is sensitive and should be separate from updating metadata/draft config.

2025-02-06 — Marcus Lin:
Agree with separating audit_log.read from audit_log_export.create. For SOC2 evidence we need to show export requires explicit permission + is logged. Also +1 on reserving system.* for support-only (non customer grantable).

2025-02-08 — Ethan Park:
Concern: introducing "cluster" scope may complicate evaluation path in control plane (we don't currently have first-class cluster membership). Suggest we model those endpoints as org scope for now, and add an attribute constraint later (e.g., dedicated_cluster_id in resource instance). If we keep cluster scope, we need to define how roles are assigned there.

2025-02-10 — Jordan Lee:
Updated proposal: keep "cluster" scope only if we can point to an actual role assignment surface. Otherwise map Dedicated infra actions to org scope + require dedicated deployment admin role. Leaving question open but leaning Ethan's direction for v0.

Also added guidance: prefer "org_member" as org__member to keep hierarchical structure consistent.

2025-02-12 — Brian Murphy:
API naming feedback:
- Prefer "list" folded into read (read covers get/list), OK.
- For secrets: "secret.read" should be metadata-only; actual secret material access should be separate (e.g., secret.reveal) if we ever allow it. For now, our APIs return masked values, so read is fine.
- For API keys: rotate/revoke are good explicit verbs; create should be separate from update.

If we proceed with double-underscore for subresource, document it clearly with examples.

2025-02-18 — Jordan Lee:
Marked In Review. Action needed: resolve Dedicated scope question (cluster vs org) and then I’ll paste final taxonomy section into the Confluence RBAC v2 overview + update ENG-5382 mapping notes.
